q: A detectable change in the internal or external environment which influences a temporary increase of physiological activity is called a _____.
e: Stimulus ဆိုသည်မှာ internal သို့မဟုတ် external environment တွင် သိရှိနိုင်သော ပြောင်းလဲမှုဖြစ်သည်။

q: In plants, coordination and response are undertaken by chemicals called _____.
e: Plants တွင် nervous system မရှိသဖြင့် coordination ကို plant hormones သို့မဟုတ် phytohormones က ဆောင်ရွက်သည်။

q: The responses to external stimuli produced by the working of various organs in a systematic and controlled manner are known as _____.
e: Coordination သည် external stimuli ကို systematic နှင့် controlled တုံ့ပြန်ခြင်းဖြစ်သည်။

q: The process of development occurs in an ordered fashion within a single diploid cell called a _____.
e: Development သည် zygote ဟုခေါ်သော diploid cell တစ်ခုမှ စတင်သည်။

q: Plants respond to environmental stimuli such as abiotic or biotic stress, and examples of plant responses include tropisms and responses to _____.
e: Plants ၏ environmental stimuli တုံ့ပြန်မှုတွင် tropisms, touch, herbivory နှင့် abiotic stress ပါဝင်သည်။

q: The movement of plant parts is due to various external and internal stimuli, where internal stimuli or internal control are chemicals called _____.
e: Plants တွင် internal stimuli သည် plant hormones ခေါ် chemicals ဖြစ်သည်။

q: Growth can be defined as an irreversible increase in size of an individual cell or organ that occurs as a result of all the _____ activities.
e: Growth သည် nutrition မှ energy သုံးသော metabolic activities အားလုံး၏ ရလဒ်ဖြစ်သည်။

q: The meristematic phase of growth occurs in the meristematic regions, where the cells are isodiametric, thin walled, and consist of a large nucleus and dense _____.
e: Meristematic cells တွင် large nucleus နှင့် dense cytoplasm ရှိသည်။

q: In the elongation phase of plant growth, the cells found around the meristematic cells are highly _____.
e: Elongation phase ရှိ cells သည် highly vacuolated ဖြစ်သည်။

q: Water is essential for enzymatic activities in protoplasm and cell elongation, while _____ is necessary for cellular respiration to produce metabolic energy.
e: Oxygen သည် growth အတွက် metabolic energy ထုတ်ရန် cellular respiration အတွက် လိုအပ်သည်။

q: Life cycle of an organism consists of a sequence of changes which are collectively called _____.
e: Development သည် organism ၏ life cycle တွင် ပြောင်းလဲမှုအစဉ်ဖြစ်သည်။

q: Phytohormones are generally synthesized at the apices of root, stem and in _____.
e: Phytohormones ကို roots, stems ၏ apices နှင့် leaves တွင် synthesize လုပ်သည်။

q: Growth promoters include auxin, gibberellin and cytokinin, while growth inhibitors include ethylene and _____ which can induce dormancy.
e: Ethylene နှင့် abscisic acid သည် dormancy ဖြစ်စေနိုင်သော growth inhibitors ဖြစ်သည်။

q: Chemically, the first plant growth regulator auxin is known as _____ acid.
e: Chemically အားဖြင့် auxin သည် indole acetic acid (IAA) ဖြစ်သည်။

q: Application of auxin to unpollinated pistil makes them develop seedless fruits, a process known as _____.
e: Parthenocarpy သည် auxin သုံးခြင်းကြောင့် seedless fruits ဖြစ်ပေါ်ခြင်းဖြစ်သည်။

q: Gibberellins promote seed germination by stimulating the synthesis of hydrolytic enzymes like amylases and _____.
e: Gibberellins က germination အတွင်း amylases နှင့် proteases ကဲ့သို့ hydrolytic enzymes ကို လှုံ့ဆော်သည်။

q: Cytokinin is a basic hormone and purine derivative that primarily acts on cell division, and a rich natural source of it is _____.
e: Coconut milk သည် cytokinins ၏ ကြွယ်ဝသော natural source ဖြစ်သည်။

q: The only gaseous phytohormone produced naturally in plants from the amino acid methionine is _____.
e: Ethylene သည် methionine မှ ထုတ်သော တစ်ခုတည်းသော gaseous phytohormone ဖြစ်သည်။

q: Abscisic acid is also known as a stress hormone because it is produced naturally when a plant is exposed to stress such as lack of water or _____ soils.
e: Abscisic acid ကို saline soils သို့မဟုတ် cold temperatures ကဲ့သို့ stress conditions တွင် ထုတ်သည်။

q: The internal inhibition of germination of a normal or viable seed even when placed under favourable conditions is called seed _____.
e: Seed dormancy သည် favourable conditions တွင်ပင် germination ၏ internal inhibition ဖြစ်သည်။

q: The dormancy of seeds can be broken by scarification, stratification, and _____ treatment.
e: Seed dormancy ကို hormonal treatment စသည့် နည်းလမ်းများဖြင့် ချိုးဖျက်နိုင်သည်။

q: During seed germination, the food present in the seed is mobilized by the activation of enzymes and the _____ grows first.
e: Radicle သည် seed germination အတွင်း ပထမဆုံးကြီးထွားသော အပိုင်းဖြစ်သည်။

q: Epigeal germination takes place above the ground because the cotyledons are pushed up by the rapid elongation of the _____.
e: Epigeal germination တွင် hypocotyl လျင်မြန်စွာ ရှည်ထွက်ပြီး cotyledons ကို မြေပေါ်သို့ တွန်းတင်သည်။

q: Vivipary is the germination of seeds inside the fruit while still attached to the parent tree, seen in plants like Agave and _____.
e: Mangroves နှင့် Agave သည် vivipary germination ပြသသည်။

q: The effect or requirements of relative length of day and night on flowering is called _____.
e: Photoperiodism သည် day နှင့် night ၏ relative length က flowering အပေါ် သက်ရောက်မှုဖြစ်သည်။

q: Short day plants require a shorter photoperiod than their critical photoperiod to initiate flowering, and an example of a short day plant is the _____.
e: Soybean နှင့် onion သည် short day plants ၏ ဥပမာများဖြစ်သည်။

q: Day neutral plants are indeterminate plants where floral initiation is independent of photoperiodism, such as the _____ plant.
e: Tomato နှင့် cotton သည် day neutral plants ဖြစ်သည်။

q: It is proposed that a hormone called _____ is synthesized in leaves and is responsible for the initiation of flowering.
e: Florigen သည် leaves တွင် synthesize လုပ်ပြီး flowering အတွက် တာဝန်ရှိသော hormone ဖြစ်သည်။

q: In the dark, plants exhibit elongated stems and undifferentiated chloroplasts, but light induces a process involving inhibition of stem elongation and differentiation of chloroplasts called _____.
e: Photomorphogenesis တွင် chloroplasts ၏ differentiation နှင့် light တွင် stem elongation inhibition ပါဝင်သည်။

q: The photomorphogenesis stimulus is perceived in leaves by a blue-green pigment protein containing a covalently attached chromophore called _____.
e: Phytochrome သည် photomorphogenesis stimulus ကို သိရှိသော blue-green pigment protein ဖြစ်သည်။

q: In plants, the maturation phase of growth involves cells undergoing structural and functional differentiation to develop into a specialized _____.
e: Maturation phase ရှိ cells သည် specialized tissues အဖြစ် differentiate ဖြစ်သည်။

q: Mineral nutrition is required for plant growth as it serves as a raw material for the synthesis of protoplasm as well as a source of _____.
e: Mineral nutrition သည် protoplasm synthesis နှင့် energy အတွက် raw material ပေးသည်။

q: Coordination involves two main body systems: the endocrine system and the _____ system, which is involved in the transmission of nerve impulses.
e: Nervous system က coordination အတွက် nerve impulses ပို့သည်။

q: The central nervous system is composed of the spinal cord and the _____.
e: CNS တွင် brain နှင့် spinal cord ပါဝင်သည်။

q: The forebrain comprises the cerebrum, thalamus, and hypothalamus, while the hindbrain consists of the cerebellum, pons, and _____.
e: Hindbrain တွင် cerebellum, pons နှင့် medulla oblongata ပါဝင်သည်။

q: The meninges are three layers of tough, elastic tissue within the skull and spinal column that directly enclose and _____ the brain and spinal cord.
e: Meninges က brain နှင့် spinal cord ကို ဝိုင်းရံကာကွယ်သည်။

q: The thalamus acts as the great _____ station of the brain, providing connections between various parts of the brain.
e: Thalamus ကို brain ၏ great relay station ဟု သိကြသည်။

q: The hypothalamus helps regulate the body's internal environment and acts as a major link between the nervous and _____ systems.
e: Hypothalamus က nervous နှင့် endocrine systems ကို ဆက်သွယ်သည်။

q: The midbrain plays an important role in eye movement and control of skeletal muscles, and relays visual and _____ information.
e: Midbrain က visual နှင့် auditory information ကို relay လုပ်သည်။

q: The cerebellum is involved in the unconscious coordination of posture, reflexes, and fine, voluntary _____ skills.
e: Cerebellum က fine, voluntary motor skills ကို coordinate လုပ်သည်။

q: The medulla oblongata coordinates automatic bodily functions that maintain homeostasis, including heart rate and the rate and depth of _____.
e: Medulla oblongata က breathing ၏ rate နှင့် depth ကဲ့သို့ automatic functions ကို ထိန်းချုပ်သည်။

q: A cross section of the spinal cord reveals an outer white matter consisting of myelinated nerve fibres and a butterfly-shaped core of _____ matter.
e: Spinal cord ၏ အတွင်း butterfly-shaped core သည် grey matter ဖြစ်သည်။

q: The somatic nervous system is under voluntary control and includes 12 pairs of cranial nerves and _____ pairs of spinal nerves.
e: Somatic nervous system တွင် spinal nerves ၃၁ စုံပါဝင်သည်။

q: An exception among cranial nerves is the _____ nerve, which connects to many internal organs including the heart, lungs, and digestive tract.
e: Vagus nerve က internal organs များစွာနှင့် ဆက်သွယ်သည်။

q: Sudden, involuntary responses to certain stimuli that enable the body to react rapidly in times of danger are called _____.
e: Reflexes သည် stimuli သို့ sudden, involuntary responses ဖြစ်သည်။

q: Reflex arcs are simple connections of only three neurones to transmit messages, allowing reflexes to occur rapidly in about _____ $	ext{ms}$.
e: Reflexes သည် $50\text{ ms}$ ခန့် အလွန်မြန်စွာ ဖြစ်သည်။

q: The sympathetic nervous system is typically activated in stressful situations, releasing a neurotransmitter called _____ which has an excitatory effect.
e: Sympathetic neurones က norepinephrine ထုတ်သည်။

q: The parasympathetic nervous system acts to restore and conserve energy, and uses the neurotransmitter _____ to control organ responses.
e: Parasympathetic system က acetylcholine သုံးသည်။

q: The nervous system is composed of neurones and cells that support them, which are collectively called _____ cells.
e: Glial cells က neurones ကို support နှင့် nourish လုပ်သည်။

q: Dendrites are short, branching terminals that receive nerve impulses, while the _____ conducts impulses away from the cell body.
e: Axon က cell body မှ impulses ကို ဝေးရာသို့ ပို့သည်။

q: The axons of some neurones are enclosed in a fatty, insulating layer called the myelin sheath, which is made up of _____ cells.
e: Myelin sheath ကို Schwann cells ဖြင့် ဖွဲ့စည်းသည်။

q: Structurally, a multipolar neurone has several dendrites and a single axon, and is typically found in the _____.
e: Multipolar neurones ကို brain နှင့် spinal cord တွင် တွေ့ရသည်။

q: Bipolar neurones have a single main dendrite and a single axon, and are found in the inner ear, the retina, and the _____ area of the brain.
e: Bipolar neurones ကို brain ၏ olfactory area တွင် တွေ့ရသည်။

q: Functionally, interneurones are found entirely within the central nervous system and act as a link between sensory and _____ neurones.
e: Interneurones က sensory နှင့် motor neurones ကို ချိတ်ဆက်သည်။

q: The connection between two neurones, or a neurone and an effector, is called a _____.
e: Synapse သည် neurones နှစ်ခု သို့မဟုတ် neurone နှင့် effector အကြား ချိတ်ဆက်မှုဖြစ်သည်။

q: Chemical messengers called neurotransmitters carry the neural signal across the synapse, taking about $0.5$ to _____ $	ext{ms}$ to reach the postsynaptic membrane.
e: Neurotransmitters က synapse ကို ဖြတ်ရန် $0.5$ မှ $1\text{ ms}$ ခန့် ကြာသည်။

q: If a neurotransmitter is excitatory, it triggers ion channels to allow positive ions like _____ to flow into the postsynaptic neurone.
e: Excitatory neurotransmitters က sodium ions ဝင်စီးခွင့်ပေးသည်။

q: If a neurotransmitter is inhibitory, it triggers channels to allow potassium ions to flow out, resulting in a more negative membrane potential called _____.
e: Inhibitory neurotransmitters က hyperpolarization ဖြစ်စေသည်။

q: Excessive production of the neurotransmitter dopamine is linked to _____, a disorder where perception of reality is greatly distorted.
e: Excessive dopamine ကို schizophrenia နှင့် ဆက်စပ်သည်။

q: Inadequate amounts of the neurotransmitter _____ in the brain synapses are linked to depression.
e: Inadequate serotonin ကို depression နှင့် ဆက်စပ်သည်။

q: Endorphins act as natural painkillers in the brain, and a deficiency is linked to an increased risk of _____.
e: Endorphin deficiency ကို alcoholism အန္တရာယ် တိုးခြင်းနှင့် ဆက်စပ်သည်။

q: The somatic nervous system's sensory neurones carry information from receptors in the skin, tendons, and skeletal muscles, while its motor neurones carry information to the _____ muscles.
e: Somatic motor neurones က skeletal muscles သို့ အချက်အလက်ပို့သည်။

q: Unipolar neurones have a single process that extends from the cell body, where the dendrite and axon are fused, and are found in the _____ nervous system.
e: Unipolar neurones ကို peripheral nervous system တွင် တွေ့ရသည်။

q: Sense organs are organs in which sensory receptors are highly concentrated to convert stimuli into electrical signals or _____.
e: Sensory receptors က stimuli ကို electrical signals သို့မဟုတ် action potentials အဖြစ် ပြောင်းသည်။

q: The outermost coat of the eyeball is the sclera, which is tough, fibrous, opaque, and protects the eye from _____ injuries.
e: Sclera က eye ကို physical injuries မှ ကာကွယ်သည်။

q: Light enters the eye through the cornea, which is a transparent layer continuous with the sclera that _____ the light rays.
e: Cornea က eye ထဲဝင်သော light rays ကို refract လုပ်သည်။

q: The middle coat of the eyeball is the choroid, which contains a black pigment that absorbs light and prevents internal _____ of light.
e: Choroid ၏ black pigment က light ၏ internal reflection ကို တားဆီးသည်။

q: The ciliary body is a thickened region at the front end of the choroid that changes the thickness of the lens during _____.
e: Ciliary body က accommodation အတွင်း lens thickness ကို ပြောင်းသည်။

q: The iris contains circular muscles and radial muscles that change the size of the pupil, and contains pigments that give the eye its _____.
e: Iris ရှိ pigments က eye အရောင်ပေးသည်။

q: The innermost layer of the eye is the retina, which consists of cone cells and rod cells that act as a screen for the formation of _____.
e: Retina သည် images ဖြစ်ပေါ်ရန် screen အဖြစ် လုပ်ဆောင်သည်။

q: The fovea, or yellow spot, contains only cone cells and provides the clearest vision, while the _____ does not contain any photoreceptors.
e: Blind spot တွင် photoreceptors မရှိပါ။

q: The flexible biconvex crystalline structure behind the iris is the lens, which divides the eye into the aqueous chamber and the _____ chamber.
e: Lens က eye ကို aqueous နှင့် vitreous chambers အဖြစ် ပိုင်းခြားသည်။

q: The aqueous humour is a clear watery fluid that maintains internal pressure and provides nutrients for the lens and _____.
e: Aqueous humour က lens နှင့် cornea အတွက် nutrients ပေးသည်။

q: The suspensory ligament attaches the lens to the ciliary body and assists the lens to change its thickness during _____.
e: Suspensory ligament က accommodation အတွင်း lens thickness ပြောင်းရန် ကူညီသည်။

q: When the eye focuses on a distant object, the ciliary muscles relax and the pressure in the eye pushes outwards, stretching the suspensory ligaments and making the lens _____.
e: Distant objects အတွက် lens သည် flat ဖြစ်လာသည်။

q: When focusing on a nearby object, the ciliary muscles contract, the suspensory ligaments become slack, and the elastic lens bulges outwards into a more _____ shape.
e: Nearby objects အတွက် lens သည် ပို convex ဖြစ်လာသည်။

q: In bright light, the pupil constricts because the circular muscles contract and the radial muscles _____.
e: Bright light တွင် radial muscles relax ဖြစ်ပြီး pupil ကို constrict လုပ်သည်။

q: In dim light, the pupil dilates because the _____ muscles contract and the circular muscles relax.
e: Dim light တွင် radial muscles contract ဖြစ်ပြီး pupil ကို dilate လုပ်သည်။

q: Endocrine glands secrete chemical messengers called hormones directly into the _____, which transports them throughout the body.
e: Hormones ကို bloodstream ထဲသို့ တိုက်ရိုက် secrete လုပ်သည်။

q: Steroid hormones such as testosterone, estrogen, and cortisol are _____-based, whereas water-soluble hormones include epinephrine and insulin.
e: Steroid hormones သည် lipid-based ဖြစ်သည်။

q: The hypothalamus secretes releasing and inhibiting hormones that regulate the _____ pituitary hormones.
e: Hypothalamic hormones က anterior pituitary hormones ကို ထိန်းညှိသည်။

q: Human growth hormone ($	ext{hGH}$) is secreted by the anterior pituitary and stimulates cell division, bone and muscle growth, and _____ function.
e: hGH က growth နှင့်အတူ metabolic function ကို လှုံ့ဆော်သည်။

q: Thyroid-stimulating hormone ($	ext{TSH}$) stimulates the thyroid gland to produce _____.
e: TSH က thyroxine ထုတ်လုပ်မှုကို လှုံ့ဆော်သည်။

q: Follicle-stimulating hormone ($	ext{FSH}$) stimulates the production of ova and sperm from the ovaries and testes, while luteinizing hormone ($	ext{LH}$) stimulates _____ hormone production.
e: LH က sex hormone production ကို လှုံ့ဆော်သည်။

q: Prolactin ($	ext{PRL}$) is an anterior pituitary hormone that stimulates milk production from the _____ glands.
e: Prolactin က mammary glands မှ milk production ကို လှုံ့ဆော်သည်။

q: Antidiuretic hormone ($	ext{ADH}$) is secreted by the posterior pituitary and promotes the retention of water by the _____.
e: ADH က kidneys တွင် water retention ကို မြှင့်တင်သည်။

q: Oxytocin is a posterior pituitary hormone that stimulates uterine muscle contractions and the release of milk by the _____ glands.
e: Oxytocin က mammary glands မှ milk release ကို လှုံ့ဆော်သည်။

q: Parathyroid hormone ($	ext{PTH}$) raises blood calcium levels by stimulating bone cells to release calcium and the intestine to absorb calcium from _____.
e: PTH က intestine ကို food မှ calcium စုပ်ယူရန် လှုံ့ဆော်သည်။

q: Thyroxine ($T_4$) is secreted by the thyroid gland and affects all tissues by increasing metabolic rate and regulating growth and _____.
e: Thyroxine က growth နှင့် development ကို ထိန်းညှိသည်။

q: Calcitonin targets bones and kidneys to lower blood calcium by inhibiting the release of calcium from bone and the _____ of calcium by kidneys.
e: Calcitonin က kidneys ၏ calcium reabsorption ကို inhibit လုပ်သည်။

q: Glucocorticoids, such as cortisol, are secreted by the adrenal cortex and stimulate tissues to raise blood glucose and break down _____.
e: Glucocorticoids က protein ၏ breakdown ကို လှုံ့ဆော်သည်။

q: Mineralocorticoids, such as aldosterone, promote the reabsorption of sodium and water by the _____.
e: Mineralocorticoids က kidneys တွင် sodium နှင့် water ပြန်စုပ်ရန် လုပ်ဆောင်သည်။

q: The adrenal medulla secretes epinephrine and nor-epinephrine, which are known as the fight-or-_____ hormones.
e: Epinephrine နှင့် nor-epinephrine သည် fight-or-flight hormones ဖြစ်သည်။

q: Insulin lowers blood glucose levels and promotes the formation of glycogen in the liver, whereas glucagon raises blood glucose by converting glycogen to _____.
e: Glucagon က liver glycogen ကို glucose အဖြစ် ပြောင်းသည်။

q: Estrogen stimulates uterine lining growth and promotes development of female secondary sexual characteristics, while progesterone promotes growth of the uterine lining and prevents uterine muscle _____.
e: Progesterone က uterine muscle contractions ကို တားဆီးသည်။

q: Testosterone is secreted by the testes and promotes sperm formation and development of male secondary sexual _____.
e: Testosterone က male secondary sexual characteristics ကို မြှင့်တင်သည်။

q: Both the nervous system and endocrine system coordinate the body's activities and need a stimulus to produce a response, but information in the endocrine system is transmitted as a chemical substance called a _____.
e: Endocrine system က hormones မှတဆင့် အချက်အလက်ပို့သည်။

q: The speed of transmission in the nervous system is fast, whereas in the endocrine system it is slow and determined by the speed of blood flow through the blood _____.
e: Endocrine transmission speed သည် vessels မှ blood flow ပေါ်မူတည်သည်။

q: The duration of effect in the nervous system is short-lived within milliseconds, while the endocrine system usually has effects lasting from minutes to _____.
e: Endocrine effects သည် မိနစ်မှ ရက်အထိ ကြာလေ့ရှိသည်။

q: The localization of effect in the nervous system may affect only a localized region, whereas the endocrine system may affect one or more organs in different parts of the _____.
e: Endocrine system က ခန္ဓာကိုယ်အပိုင်းအမျိုးမျိုးရှိ organs ကို သက်ရောက်နိုင်သည်။
